HGEN 400.description: Introduction to the genetic counseling profession including professional literature and online resources. Preparation for graduation education in genetic counseling.
HGEN 400.subject: HGEN
HGEN 400.title: Genetic Counseling: Career for the Future

HGEN 700.description: An overview of the role of genetics in health and illness. Focus of study includes strategies for diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of genetic disease and the integration of genetics into clinical practice.
HGEN 700.subject: HGEN
HGEN 700.title: Medical Genetics for Health Professionals

HGEN 701.description: An overview of the history and development of genetic counseling. Introduction to the fundamental components of and skills utilized in prenatal, pediatric, and adult genetic counseling.
HGEN 701.subject: HGEN
HGEN 701.title: Introduction to Genetic Counseling

HGEN 702.description: Exploration of the impact of genetic conditions on the individual and family. Psychosocial skills will be strengthened through reading, role play, discussion, and interactions with affected individuals and families.
HGEN 702.subject: HGEN
HGEN 702.title: Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Counseling

HGEN 703.description: Seminar in bioethical principles and their application to case management and genetic counseling. Includes lecture, case presentation, and discussion.
HGEN 703.subject: HGEN
HGEN 703.title: Approaches to Ethical Challenges in Genetic Counseling

HGEN 704.description: Introduction to counseling skills utilized in genetic counseling via reading, discussion, clinical observation, and role play.
HGEN 704.subject: HGEN
HGEN 704.title: The Genetic Counseling Process

HGEN 705.description: Intensive skill development focused on practical aspects of patient care for clinical rotation preparation.
HGEN 705.subject: HGEN
HGEN 705.title: Clinical Skills Seminar

HGEN 710.description: An integration of the student’s theoretical background and clinical experiences with focus on the development of clinical skills. Format includes case presentation and discussion.
HGEN 710.subject: HGEN
HGEN 710.title: Genetic Counseling Methods

HGEN 715.description: Discussion forum targeted at critical evaluation of medical genetics literature and examination of current issues facing the genetic counseling profession. May be repeated for up to 4 credit hours.
HGEN 715.subject: HGEN
HGEN 715.title: Contemporary Issues in Genetic Counseling

HGEN 720.description: A study of the clinical aspects of human genetics with focus on single gene, chromosomal, and multifactorial genetic disease; the underlying molecular and biochemical principles; and determination of genetic risk.
HGEN 720.subject: HGEN
HGEN 720.title: Medical Genetics

HGEN 722.description: Principles of genetics as they apply to medicine and basic concepts needed to understand human genetics. Current knowledge and essential areas of research in human and medical genetics.
HGEN 722.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 302 and BIOL 303 or equivalent.
HGEN 722.subject: HGEN
HGEN 722.title: Human and Medical Genetics

HGEN 725.description: The process of normal human development and basic physiological/anatomical processes of organ systems including embryo, craniofacial, nervous, respiratory, musculoskeletal, and the integumentary systems. Clinical significance andetiologies of human malformations.
HGEN 725.subject: HGEN
HGEN 725.title: Human Developmental Biology I

HGEN 726.description: Systems covered include cardiac, vascular, and urogenital. Additional topics include clinical correlates, ultrasound, labod and delivery, infancy, childhood, and adolescence.
HGEN 726.subject: HGEN
HGEN 726.title: Human Developmental Biology II

HGEN 730.description: A comprehensive seminar series taught by clinical geneticists, genetic counselors, and health care practitioners. Topics include a broad range of medical conditions with underlying genetic etiologies, genetic testing methodologies used to diagnose these conditions and therapies/treatments currently available for medical management of these conditions.
HGEN 730.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in HGEN 720.
HGEN 730.subject: HGEN
HGEN 730.title: Advanced Medical Genetics I

HGEN 731.description: A comprehensive seminar series taught by clinical geneticists, genetic counselors, and health care practitioners. Topics include a broad range of medical conditions with underlying genetic etiologies, genetic testing methodologies used to diagnose these conditions and therapies/treatments currently available for medical management of these conditions.
HGEN 731.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in HGEN 730.
HGEN 731.subject: HGEN
HGEN 731.title: Advanced Medical Genetics II

HGEN 735.description: Overview of medical oncology with an emphasis on familial and hereditary cancer. Includes didactic lectures, oral and written assignments.
HGEN 735.subject: HGEN
HGEN 735.title: Cancer Genetics and Genetic Counseling

HGEN 740.description: Foundation for beginning health professions students to gain an understanding of the complexities of the health care system through experiential activities conducted in interprofessional teams and the importance of interprofessional collaboration in order to improve the system. Also graded pass/fail for pharmacy, social work and public health, other units with stand-alone course (medicine and nursing have requirements embedded in larger class).
HGEN 740.subject: HGEN
HGEN 740.title: Transforming Health Care for the Future

HGEN 750.description: Clinical placement in a regional genetic center under direct supervision of geneticist/genetic counselor. Allows opportunity for development of genetic counseling skills as students begin transition from theory to practice.
HGEN 750.subject: HGEN
HGEN 750.title: Summer Clinical Rotation

HGEN 760.description: Two days per week of clinical placement under direct supervision of geneticist/genetic counselor for experience in prenatal, pediatric, and disease-specific clinics.
HGEN 760.subject: HGEN
HGEN 760.title: Clinical Rotation I

HGEN 761.description: Two days per week of clinical placement under direct supervision of geneticist/genetic counselor for experience in prenatal, pediatric, and disease-specific clinics.
HGEN 761.subject: HGEN
HGEN 761.title: Clinical Rotation II
